title: Obsidian / gold fault lines
positive: A physically rendered sculptural bust of the Hindu goddess Durga in polished midnight-black obsidian, placed on the LEFT third of a wide composition and turned slightly toward the right. Her entire modest stepped crown is visible. Fine gold kintsugi seams trace the stone surface like elegant geological veins. Calm sculpted eyes with subtle gold inlay, carved lips, a small gold nose ring. The bust ends in a smooth draped stone pedestal, no arms in frame. Behind her, enormous thin elliptical brass rings float diagonally across empty charcoal space. One narrow warm rim light, tactile volcanic stone, subtle gold reflections, monumental gallery installation, cinematic ray-traced product rendering. Restrained palette of black and molten gold, asymmetrical composition. A respectful contemporary artistic interpretation of Ma Durga, serene, beautiful and powerful. Two carefully matched natural almond eyes with aligned pupils, plus one small distinct vertical third eye centered on the forehead. Fully clothed. Panoramic 104:45 composition, a clear face readable on an LED wall, generous breathing room. No lettering.
